item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of GitHub Spark on github.com
item.description:
GitHub Spark will stop accepting new users and new app creation starting August 4, 2026. Existing users can keep using Spark until August 31, 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize Dependabot pull request branch names
item.description:
Dependabot now supports custom pull request branch names through new pull-request-branch-name settings in .github/dependabot.yml. You can configure a prefix, maximum length, and separators for segments and words.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.2 adds Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.2 has been released with support for Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize the reasoning level for Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Copilot cloud agent now lets you set the reasoning level for supported models when delegating a task. This gives you control over how much reasoning the agent uses for a request.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise team specialization for managed settings
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now apply managed settings using itemized configuration files targeted at enterprise teams. This lets large organizations delegate more specific governance without routing every change through central admins or relying on a single global configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Trusted Launch as Default
item.description:
Trusted Launch as Default is now generally available for new Azure Gen2 virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets. It automatically enables Secure Boot and vTPM for supported deployments.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Trigger Copilot automations with comments
item.description:
GitHub now supports triggering Copilot cloud agent automations from new issue comments and pull request comments. This enables comment-based workflows such as generating documentation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Strengthening NuGet Supply Chain Security: Reducing API Key Lifetime
item.description:
NuGet API key lifetimes will be reduced to 30 days starting August 17, with the goal of improving supply chain security.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Triage role can bypass issue creation restrictions
item.description:
GitHub changed issue creation restrictions so users with the triage role can now create issues in repositories where issue creation is limited to collaborators only. Previously, only users with write access could create issues under that setting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Immutability to the most recent seven days of backups on Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
item.description:
Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance now automatically apply immutability to the most recent seven days of backups. The feature is enabled by default for all databases, regardless of the configured point-in-time restore retention.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Migrate from GitLab to GitHub with GitHub Enterprise Importer
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Importer now generally supports self-serve migrations from gitlab.com and GitLab Self-Managed to GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The feature is available through GEI and the GitHub CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Gateway API v1.6: TCPRoute and UDPRoute Graduate to Standard
item.description:
Gateway API v1.6.0 promotes TCPRoute and UDPRoute to Standard/v1, adding GA-level raw TCP and UDP routing. It also moves experimental APIs into a separate gateway.networking.x-k8s.io group with X-prefixed kinds to make the experimental boundary explicit.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Single-click purchase for public SaaS offers
item.description:
Eligible SaaS products in Microsoft Marketplace now support a single-page purchase flow in the Azure portal. Buyers can review plan, billing, resource group, contact details, and terms before completing the purchase.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Upcoming August 2026 model deprecations in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot will deprecate several models across all Copilot experiences on September 1, 2026. The affected experiences include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, has been compromising sign-in portals at hospitality organizations since May 2026 to deliver malware to travelers and steal credentials. The campaign is named CaptiveCrunch and targets travelers worldwide.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Route-Maps for Azure Route Server
item.description:
Route maps for Azure Route Server are in public preview. They let customers control inbound and outbound routing on hybrid connections by managing routes advertised to and from Azure Route Server BGP peerings.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash deprecated
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash across all Copilot experiences as of July 31, 2026. This includes Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for late-July
item.description:
Azure SQL added a public preview of regex-based dynamic data masking. It extends built-in DDM with pattern-based masking for sensitive data such as emails, phone numbers, and identifiers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise teams model policy targeting in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added user-based model policy targeting for enterprise teams in public preview. It is available to GitHub Enterprise customers with Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise licenses and lets AI administrators set a baseline policy.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Restricting npm bypass-2FA granular access tokens
item.description:
npm granular access tokens configured to bypass 2FA can no longer be used for sensitive account, organization, and package management actions. Those operations now require an interactive 2FA challenge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37 Sneak Peek
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 is planning several deprecations and a few feature graduations. Notable changes include deprecating kubectl run -f, forbidding Static Pods from referencing Secrets/ConfigMaps, starting deprecation of kube-proxy ipvs mode, and moving SELinuxMount to GA with possible workload impact.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: dotnet: From generated code to trusted code with a unit-test agent
item.description:
Microsoft introduced an open-source polyglot unit-testing agent that analyzes a repository, generates unit tests, and verifies that the tests build and pass. The post focuses on moving from generated code to code that is checked and trusted through automated testing.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: devops+ai: Had baby, Back September!
item.description:
The post says the author had a baby in September and will be back later. They also note they won’t be using AI for a while.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in India South Central
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server is now generally available in the India South Central Azure region. Users can deploy new flexible server instances in that region.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Models is now retired
item.description:
GitHub Models was retired on July 30, 2026. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) access are no longer available to customers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Automation supports PowerShell 7.6 runbooks and Runtime environment
item.description:
Azure Automation now generally supports PowerShell 7.6 runbooks and the Runtime environment. This lets customers move scripts to a supported runtime version, with Azure CLI command support also mentioned in the update.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Reservation exchanges for Azure services supported by savings plans will no longer be available starting February 1, 2027
item.description:
Azure will stop allowing reservation exchanges for services covered by savings plans starting February 1, 2027. At announcement time, this applies to Azure Virtual Machine compute reservations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium
item.description:
Azure Key Vault Premium now supports symmetric keys in public preview. The preview lets customers and partners evaluate symmetric encryption using oct-HSM keys and AES.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Reference same-repository actions with self-repository syntax
item.description:
GitHub added a new self-repository syntax for uses: so actions and reusable workflows in the same repository can be referenced with a $/-prefixed value. This changes how same-repo workflows/actions are addressed, but the provided text does not include further details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Support for SMB Opportunistic Locking (Oplocks) configuration
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files public preview adds configurable SMB opportunistic locking (oplocks) for SMB and dual-protocol volumes. Oplocks remain enabled by default and can be set on new volumes or updated on existing ones.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stacked pull requests are now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has put stacked pull requests into public preview. The feature lets users split a larger change into an ordered series of smaller, reviewable pull requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: July 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s July 2026 Security update highlights new capabilities for securing AI environments, using AI for defense, and improving the underlying systems that AI-powered operations rely on. The provided excerpt does not include specific product changes or feature details.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — July update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s July 2026 update adds a new agent built on the Copilot SDK, plus built-in expertise from the .NET and Azure teams. It also adds more options to tailor Copilot to individual workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Limit remote control to managed devices
item.description:
Enterprises and organizations can now limit Copilot remote control sessions to managed devices. This adds administrator control over which devices are eligible to host remote control access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, July 2026 releases
item.description:
GitHub’s July 2026 Copilot-in-VS Code changelog covers VS Code v1.127 through v1.131. The releases focus on agent workflows, reviewing changes, chat, and navigation improvements.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Agent skills and MCP now generally available
item.description:
Copilot code review now generally supports agent skills and MCP servers for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users. These features have moved from public preview to general availability.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Monitor Logs mirroring into Microsoft Fabric
item.description:
Azure Monitor Logs can now be mirrored from Log Analytics workspaces into Microsoft Fabric in public preview. The telemetry is available in OneLake as Delta Parquet with near real-time availability and no data duplication.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available for evaluation
item.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 RC1 is available in the Retail Eval feed for evaluation. This release has no customer-facing changes, but it includes a major upgrade to the underlying Linux kernel version as part of long-term support work.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: How the controller-runtime Cache Actually Works, and Why Your Controller Does Not Crash the API Server
item.description:
The article explains that controller-runtime controllers read from a local informer cache, not directly from the API server, and that writes go to the API server while the cache catches up asynchronously via watch events. It also details how shared informers, DeltaFIFO, indexing, cache scoping, APIReader, and cache disabling affect consistency, memory use, and query behavior.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: commandline: Tool search: Finding the right tool at the right time
item.description:
The article says the value in adding more tools to AI agents comes from surfacing the right tool at the right time, instead of exposing every tool upfront. It focuses on discoverability as the key problem.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: ​​Better security starts with better questions
item.description:
Microsoft Security says stronger security decisions come from asking better questions, using trusted AI, and combining AI outputs with human judgment. The post frames this as a way to help leaders make more confident decisions and build more resilient systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Default model enablement for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default enablement policy for generally available Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. New GA models will be enabled by default instead of requiring admins to turn each one on manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.1 improves analysis accuracy and framework coverage
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.1 has been released with improvements to analysis accuracy and broader framework coverage, including Go. The changelog item is brief and does not list additional specific fixes or language/framework details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app usage metrics now expand across report rollups
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app usage metrics are now included in more of the Copilot usage metrics API. Individual app activity is now attributed to users in the enterprise-user and organization-user reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm publish-time malware scanning and dual-use metadata
item.description:
npm is adding automatic malware scanning when packages are published, along with a new metadata requirement for packages that may be used for both benign and malicious purposes. The changelog says this is part of ongoing supply-chain security work and explains what publishers should expect.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing v2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK
item.description:
The official MCP C# SDK v2.0 now implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification. It adds a stateless-first protocol, standardized HTTP headers, and Multi Round-Trip Requests for interactive tools while remaining backward compatible.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Grok 4.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.5 is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the xAI model is intended for fast, agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows, with a large context window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Enclave
item.description:
Azure Enclave is now in public preview for Microsoft Azure, Azure Government, Azure Government Secret, and Azure Government Top Secret. It is intended to simplify deployment and management of isolated cloud environments for sensitive workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: NAT64 on StandardV2 NAT Gateway
item.description:
StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports NAT64. This lets IPv6 workloads reach IPv4-only internet destinations by translating synthesized outbound IPv6 traffic to IPv4, using a DNS64-capable resolver.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Application Routing with Gateway API
item.description:
Application Routing with Gateway API is now generally available on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). It lets teams use the Kubernetes Gateway API for ingress routing while supporting existing deployments.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
item.description:
Resource placement in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager is now generally available. It lets users define where Kubernetes resources should be scheduled across multiple clusters to reduce manual work and improve consistency.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Maximum allowed failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager
item.description:
Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager now has a preview option to set a maximum number of allowed failures for update runs. In fail-fast rollouts, this lets some member cluster update failures occur without stopping the broader deployment immediately.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Prepared Image Specification
item.description:
Azure announces a public preview of Prepared Image Specification for AKS workloads that need faster node startup. The feature is aimed at reducing delays caused by repeated container image downloads and initialization on new nodes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Azure now available from new cloud region in India (India South Central)
item.description:
Microsoft has launched a new Azure datacenter region in India, India South Central, with campuses in Hyderabad, Telangana. The region is intended to provide local cloud infrastructure for customers in India.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Dependabot alerts on malicious packages across more ecosystems
item.description:
GitHub Advisory Database now ingests malware advisories from OpenSSF’s malicious-packages repository, expanding the malware data available to Dependabot alerts. This broadens coverage across more ecosystems.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions holds potentially malicious workflows for approval
item.description:
GitHub Actions now detects potentially malicious workflow changes in public repositories and requires approval before they run. The change is intended to reduce supply-chain abuse from compromised credentials used to add workflows that steal CI/CD secrets or perform follow-on attacks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now includes improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management. The update also adds support for connecting MCP servers and custom agents in Claude agent flows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage GitHub Copilot app access with a dedicated policy
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now has a dedicated policy for controlling app access at both the enterprise and organization levels. This separates Copilot app access from the previous broader access controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Claude Opus 5 on Azure Databricks
item.description:
Azure Databricks now supports Anthropic Claude Opus 5 through AI Model Serving. The update makes the model available for advanced reasoning, coding, agentic workflows, and professional knowledge work.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in the GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent now support enterprise managed settings, letting organizations apply the same centrally managed Copilot policies across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Analyze MSBuild Binary Logs with Copilot in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the MSBuild Binlog Analyzer for VS Code, a Copilot-powered tool for reading MSBuild binary logs, explaining build failures, suggesting fixes, comparing builds, and identifying regressions. It uses the Microsoft.AITools.BinlogMcp MCP server.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: HTTP header insertion in Azure Firewall
item.description:
Azure Firewall now supports inserting or overwriting HTTP/HTTPS request headers from application rules. This lets organizations enforce security controls and support tenant restriction at the firewall layer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AI Gateway in Azure API Management
item.description:
Azure API Management now has an AI Gateway tier in public preview. It is a dedicated tier designed for AI workloads, extending AI gateway capabilities already available in other API Management tiers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Enhancing AI security through global AI red teaming
item.description:
Microsoft announced EXTRA, a global AI security initiative focused on AI safety research and red teaming. The program partners with universities, researchers, and regional experts to identify emerging AI risks and improve testing of frontier AI systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: From research to reality: An interview with Microsoft VP of Security Research Taesoo Kim
item.description:
Microsoft interviewed Taesoo Kim, VP of Security Research and head of Security FORGE Labs, about codename MDASH and the lab’s work on security research. The interview highlights a multi-model, agentic approach as a potential direction for improving security capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: aks: Release 2026-07-17
item.description:
AKS v20260717 adds Artifact Streaming GA, new preview networking and scheduling features, and multiple behavior changes and bug fixes. It also updates Kubernetes patch versions, core add-ons, node images, and includes several retirement notices and upcoming defaults.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: github: Claude Opus 5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Claude Opus 5, Anthropic’s latest Opus model. GitHub says it is intended for complex, long-running coding tasks that need careful reasoning and tool use.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot cloud agent for Linear is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub says Copilot cloud agent is now generally available for Linear. Users can assign Linear issues to the agent, which then analyzes the issue contents and works asynchronously in the background.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
item.description:
GitHub MCP Server will support the upcoming MCP spec ahead of its official release. The key protocol change is a move to a stateless core on 28 July 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Mobile: Fix failing Actions checks with Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Mobile now lets you ask Copilot coding agent to investigate and fix failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request directly from the mobile app. The feature starts from a failed check and uses Copilot cloud agent to work on the issue.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multi-select fields for Projects and Issues in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Projects and Issue fields now support multi-select fields in public preview, allowing a single field to store multiple values. This lets you tag an item with all relevant labels or categories instead of choosing just one.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection custom policy
item.description:
Azure DDoS Protection custom policy is in public preview. It lets customers set per-resource DDoS mitigation thresholds for protected Standard Load Balancer frontend IP configurations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Agent automation controls in GitHub Issues in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Issues now exposes the reason behind agent-driven changes and lets users review proposed automation actions before they are applied. The feature is in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Microsoft reports that Q2 2026 saw continued declines in several phishing techniques after disruption of the Tycoon2FA platform. Attackers shifted toward Teams-based social engineering and more automated, multi-stage attack chains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Standard service endpoint
item.description:
Standard service endpoint is in public preview. It provides a more scalable and secure way to connect IaaS workloads to Azure PaaS services within the Private Link family, addressing scale and management limits of earlier approaches.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: New Copilot usage metrics impact dashboard
item.description:
GitHub released a new Copilot metrics impact dashboard for enterprise administrators and organization owners. It is meant to help them report Copilot impact using usage metrics and related data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Real world incident response: Microsoft and AXA XL strengthen cyber resilience
item.description:
Microsoft and AXA XL are collaborating to give cyber insurance policyholders direct access to Microsoft Incident Response services. The goal is to help organizations coordinate technical response, business decisions, and insurance actions during incidents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Upcoming GHES change impacting uploading support bundles
item.description:
GitHub will begin rejecting some GHES support bundle uploads starting August 18, 2026 because of an upcoming security change. Administrators should review the new upload requirements before that date to avoid failed submissions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Gemini 3.6 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Gemini 3.6 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says it is intended for web and app development, coding, and longer-horizon agentic tasks, with configurable behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: AI credit pools for cost centers in the billing UI
item.description:
GitHub Billing UI now lets you manage a cost center’s AI credit pool directly when creating or editing cost centers. Before this change, that configuration was only available through another interface.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot users can now see AI credits used per billing cycle
item.description:
Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users can now view how many AI credits they have used in the current billing cycle, even if they do not have an individual budget. The usage count is available in GitHub Copilot usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Protect sensitive generative AI telemetry in Application Insights and Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Application Insights now stores generative AI content in a dedicated GenAIContent table (AppGenAIContent in Log Analytics), enabling access controls for sensitive AI telemetry. The update is in public preview.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: IPv6 support for Azure VPN Gateway
item.description:
Azure VPN Gateway now supports IPv6 inner traffic in dual-stack VPN tunnels. The feature is available on all production SKU gateways that use standard public IPs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality is now generally available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team. The announcement says it is intended to help with the growing volume of code produced with AI assistance.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository-level GitHub Copilot usage metrics generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics REST API now includes repository-level activity. Two new endpoints provide a daily per-repository breakdown of pull request activity for Copilot coding agent and Copilot code review.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app now available in the usage metrics API
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot usage metrics API now includes GitHub Copilot app usage in enterprise and organization 1-day and 28-day reports. This adds admin visibility into Copilot app usage data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Customization and configurability improvements
item.description:
Copilot code review now supports a firewall, custom setup steps, and independent runner configurations. It also reads custom instructions from the head branch to make testing and validation easier.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Mobile: Fix pull request comments with Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Mobile now lets you select “Fix with Copilot” from Copilot code review pull request comments. The action is available in the pull request’s main view and uses the Copilot cloud agent.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions support for Python 3.14
item.description:
Azure Functions now supports Python 3.14 for local development and deployment to Linux-based Azure Functions plans. This lets apps move to Python 3.14 for security, longer support, and continued compatibility.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Public Preview: Azure Functions Support for PowerShell 7.6
item.description:
Azure Functions now supports PowerShell 7.6 in public preview. You can develop locally with PowerShell 7.6 and deploy to Azure Functions plans.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Microsoft at Black Hat USA 2026: Defending trust in the age of AI and supply chain attacks
item.description:
Microsoft Security says it will be at Black Hat USA 2026 with sessions on supply chain research, hands-on security experiences, expert conversations, and a reception. The post frames the event around trust, AI, and supply chain attacks.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
item.description:
Microsoft Defender CSPM assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server are now generally available. The assessments can be used to continuously evaluate the security posture of PostgreSQL flexible servers in Azure.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Encryption in Transit for Azure Files NFS Shares in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
item.description:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now generally supports Encryption in Transit for Azure Files NFS v4.1 volumes through the Azure File CSI driver. When enabled, data transferred between AKS workloads and Azure Files NFS shares is encrypted in transit.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ACR Stealer: Two observed intrusion chains amid increased threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft Defender Experts observed increased ACR Stealer activity from late April to mid-June 2026 across customer environments. The campaigns used ClickFix lures to steal browser credentials, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents from enterprise environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Advanced search for Projects is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Projects views now support advanced search in the filter bar. You can combine conditions with logical AND and OR to build more precise views without maintaining a separate setup.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository admins can archive pull requests
item.description:
Repository admins can archive pull requests to remove them from public view without deleting them. Archived pull requests are closed and locked.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: REST API endpoints for Visual Studio Subscription management
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud admins can now use REST API endpoints to manage Visual Studio Subscription (VSS) assignments programmatically. The new endpoint returns all VSS assignments for an enterprise, including assignment details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub-hosted macOS runners now support Xcode 27 in public preview, letting you build and test Apple apps against the latest Xcode version. This is an early-access runner image release.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing .NET Modernization for Beginners
item.description:
Microsoft announced a free, open-source hands-on course for modernizing a legacy ASP.NET application to .NET 10 using the GitHub Copilot modernization agent. The course is step-by-step and aimed at beginners.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
item.description:
Microsoft Security published a post on applying least-privilege principles to AI agents, focusing on identity, access control, tool binding, and auditing as agents become more autonomous.

item.title: azure: Announcing: GitHub Copilot and Claude Code connectors in Microsoft Agent Framework
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework now includes generally available connectors for GitHub Copilot and Claude Code. These connectors let .NET and Python agents delegate coding tasks to either system without custom adapter code.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration patterns including Magentic in Microsoft Agent Framework
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework is now generally available for multi-agent orchestration patterns, including the dynamic Magentic pattern. The announcement cites benchmark results for Magentic, including 38% on GAIA and competitive results on AssistantBench and WebArena.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Agent Harness in Microsoft Agent Framework
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework now has general availability for Agent Harness, the production runtime for agents built with the framework. Preview harness users can move the same agent code into production with backward compatibility.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration SDK with the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework in C# and Python
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry has introduced Agent Framework, a unified multi-agent orchestration SDK for C# and Python. It consolidates orchestration patterns previously split across AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a single set of abstractions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Tracing for Microsoft Agent Framework (Python and .NET)
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now provides public preview tracing support for Microsoft Agent Framework in Python and .NET. The feature lets developers observe agent reasoning, tool calls, and model interactions during execution.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: CodeAct pattern and Hyperlight containers in Microsoft Agent Framework
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework now includes the CodeAct pattern in public preview. It lets agents execute multi-step plans as a single code block instead of sequential tool calls, which reduced end-to-end latency in representative workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Episodic procedural memory in Microsoft Agent Framework
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework now has episodic procedural memory in public preview. It stores successful task patterns so agents can reuse past action sequences, tool choices, and related context on similar future requests.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Agent Channel for Microsoft Agent Framework multi-agent communication
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework now includes Agent Channel in public preview for multi-agent communication. It provides a built-in way for agents to exchange typed messages using request/response or fire-and-forget patterns without custom routing code.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.description:
Azure SQL added Shortcut Configuration in Visual Studio Code preview, allowing users to customize keyboard shortcuts for Quick Queries, the Results Grid, and the Query Editor. The update is listed as a public preview for mid-July 2026.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.description:

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Advanced platform metrics in Azure Monitor
item.description:

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — June update
item.description:
June 2026’s Visual Studio Copilot update focuses on usage visibility, a new trust layer for MCP servers, and the first C++ scenarios. The post emphasizes controls and clarity rather than new broad functionality.

GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports expanded bring-your-own-key (BYOK) customization across all Copilot tiers, with broader model provider flexibility and improved plugin/provider experiences. The update also includes changes to conversational interactions in the IDE.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Front Door edge actions
item.description:
Azure Front Door edge actions are now in public preview. They let customers run lightweight JavaScript during request processing at the edge for real-time decisions closer to users.

item.title: github: Code scanning shows AI security detections on pull requests
item.description:

item.description:

item.title: security: Microsoft named a leader in the Frost Radar for cloud and application runtime security
item.description:
Microsoft says Frost & Sullivan named it a leader in the Frost Radar for cloud and application runtime security. The post frames this as recognition for a unified approach to cloud and application security focused on runtime risk reduction.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Client-side data integrity protections in Azure Blob Storage
item.description:
Azure Blob Storage now includes CRC64-NVME client-side data integrity protections in the latest Azure Blob SDKs for .NET, C++, and JavaScript. This builds on existing MD5 and server-side integrity validation support.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes are now generally available. They provide a unified endpoint for commonly used tools in prompt agents and can also be invoked outside prompt agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Accelerating the quantum-safe timeline
item.description:
Microsoft says it is accelerating quantum-safe readiness and urging organizations to begin transitioning earlier as the perceived risk timeline shifts. The post is a brief announcement pointing readers to guidance on what can be done now.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Claude Sonnet 5 is generally available for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Sonnet 5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it offers strong coding performance for everyday development and agentic workflows as a new Sonnet-class model option.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: MCP Beyond the Chat Window: Build Diagnostics in CI
item.description:
Microsoft’s .NET blog describes using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for build diagnostics in CI, including the full Binlog MCP toolset and how it runs in a GitHub Actions workflow. It also reports evaluation data on efficiency gains from this approach.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub code coverage merge protection for pull requests
item.description:
GitHub added branch ruleset support to block pull request merges when code coverage falls below a threshold you configure. You can set coverage-based merge requirements to enforce a minimum percentage and limit coverage decreases.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Releases: Sidebar navigation and per-asset download counts
item.description:
GitHub Releases now include a dedicated sidebar table of contents for easier navigation, and release metadata has been rearranged for a more consistent layout. Per-asset download counts are also shown on release pages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot Agent is now available in JetBrains AI Assistant
item.description:
GitHub and JetBrains announced a deeper integration between JetBrains AI Assistant and GitHub Copilot. Copilot Agent is now available inside JetBrains AI Assistant.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Open source license compliance is in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has put open source license compliance into public preview for enterprises. The feature adds centralized, ruleset-based checks to enforce dependency license policy and block noncompliant licenses.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s June 2026 security update post says the month’s changes focus on identity and multicloud foundations, data protection across locations, and securing developer workflows for AI-related work. The provided excerpt does not include product-level details or specific feature announcements.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
item.description:
The post explains MCP tool poisoning as an attack that can turn trusted AI agents into a control plane for data loss. It describes how attackers manipulate tool descriptions to induce unauthorized actions, and outlines detection, containment, and prevention approaches.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Dependabot no longer infers .npmrc
item.description:
Dependabot no longer infers .npmrc settings for npm private registries. Instead of reconstructing .npmrc from lockfile URLs, it will stop trying to guess configuration based on potentially incorrect lockfile data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming cloud data retention policy for closed security alerts
item.description:
GitHub will begin enforcing a cloud data retention policy for closed Dependabot security alerts on August 25, 2026. The post says this provides a defined retention period for alert data, but it does not include the exact duration in the excerpt provided.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Per-user AI credit budgets available for cost centers
item.description:
Enterprise admins can now assign a per-user AI credit budget to a cost center, with the budget applying to each individual member. The budget updates as cost center membership changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: .NET 8 and .NET 9 will reach End of Support on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says .NET 8 and .NET 9 will both reach end of support on November 10, 2026. The post directs users to upgrade to .NET 10, which is the next LTS release.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: SkiaSharp 4.0 is here: announcing the first stable release
item.description:
SkiaSharp 4.148.0 is the first stable release of SkiaSharp v4. The post says it covers what’s new in this release and references a live event on June 30.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Packaging and Package Identity for .NET apps with WinApp CLI on Windows
item.description:
Microsoft describes using the WinApp CLI to add package identity and create packages for .NET desktop apps on Windows. This enables deeper Windows integration and simpler distribution.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) is now in preview for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Claude Opus 4.8 in preview with fast mode enabled. GitHub says fast mode increases output token speed while keeping the same model intelligence.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Chromium extension uses AI‑related branding to redirect browser search
item.description:
Microsoft reports a malicious Chromium extension that used AI-related branding to impersonate Perplexity AI and redirect browser search traffic. The extension relied on MV3 APIs and intermediary infrastructure to steer searches away from intended destinations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Restrict issue creation to collaborators only
item.description:
Repository admins can now limit issue creation to collaborators with write access. This adds control over who can open issues and helps reduce unwanted issue creation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track total merges by adoption phase in enterprise and organization reports
item.description:
GitHub enterprise and organization reports now include the total number of pull requests merged by each AI adoption phase cohort. This extends the adoption phase metrics previously added to the Copilot usage metrics API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Read-only Actions cache for untrusted triggers
item.description:
GitHub Actions now uses read-only cache tokens on the default branch for workflow events that can be triggered without repository write permissions. This narrows cache access for untrusted triggers by applying least privilege.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Open source maintainership in the age of AI
item.description:
Kubernetes says AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but maintainers must keep human accountability, transparency, and verification at the center. The community is also testing AI review tools such as Copilot and CodeRabbit to help with pull request review and maintainer workload.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1-Flash for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise
item.description:
MAI-Code-1-Flash, Microsoft AI’s in-house coding model, is now generally available for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise. It builds on its recent expansion across Copilot surfaces and is described as purpose-built for coding and optimized.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Desktop 3.6: Worktrees and deeper Copilot integration
item.description:
GitHub Desktop 3.6 adds Git worktree support and expands GitHub Copilot integration for commit authoring and merge conflict resolution. It brings more of the Git workflow into Desktop.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release - 2026-06-19
item.description:
AKS 2026-06-19 adds Kubernetes 1.36 GA/LTS, Application Gateway for Containers GA, and several platform updates including FIPS on Ubuntu 22.04, CVM with Azure Linux GA, and multiple CSI/CNI/component patch upgrades. It also changes some defaults and validations, including Istio CNI behavior for new asm-1-30 installs, dual-stack IPv6 CIDR derivation, and stricter checks for gMSA and FIPS/Kata combinations.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: security: Photo ZIP campaign targeting hospitality industry delivers Node.js implant for persistent access
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported an active multi-stage intrusion campaign targeting hospitality organizations in Europe and Asia. The attackers use photo-themed ZIP archives and fake image shortcut files to deploy a persistent Node.js implant and avoid detection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: k8s: Introducing the Cluster API plugin for Headlamp
item.description:
Headlamp now has an alpha Cluster API plugin that adds visual management and debugging views for CAPI resources inside the UI. It covers cluster health, resource hierarchies, scaling, bootstrap config inspection, topology awareness, map view, and inline Prometheus metrics support.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Analysis depth and efficiency updates
item.description:
Copilot code review now uses built-in file exploration tools from the Copilot CLI and SDK. GitHub says this improves review cost efficiency without changing the existing workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support strictKnownMarketplaces in VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed support for strictKnownMarketplaces in VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI. The setting is in public preview and lets enterprises control which plugins users can install.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Inspect Volcano workloads faster with Headlamp
item.description:
The Volcano plugin for Headlamp adds dedicated views for Volcano Jobs, Queues, and PodGroups, plus a map view that shows how they relate to Pods and events. It is meant to improve interactive troubleshooting and inspection of batch workloads without replacing kubectl or the Volcano CLI.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Saved views for repository issues – Public Preview and adjustable row heights in projects
item.description:
GitHub added saved views to repository Issues pages in public preview, allowing teams to create and share filtered issue views. The release also includes adjustable row heights in Projects.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: More control over your GitHub-hosted runners
item.description:
GitHub Actions org admins can now control access to GitHub-hosted runners more tightly. They can disable standard hosted-runner labels like ubuntu-latest and add custom labels for finer-grained usage control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: See your serverless: introducing the Headlamp plugin for Knative
item.description:
Headlamp now has a Knative plugin that adds integrated views and actions for Knative resources in the Kubernetes UI. It centralizes KService management, traffic splitting, autoscaling configuration, metrics, and related CRDs, with release 0.3.0-beta available.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Actions steps can now be run in parallel
item.description:
GitHub Actions now supports running workflow steps concurrently by running them in the background. Previously, steps always executed sequentially, with each step waiting for the prior one to finish.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm adds preventive account protection for high-impact accounts
item.description:
npm now applies a temporary preventive safeguard to high-impact accounts when it detects sensitive account changes. The measure is intended to reduce account-takeover risk for maintainers of widely used packages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Migrate from Azure Blueprints by January 31, 2027
item.description:
Azure Blueprints retirement has been extended from July 11, 2026 to January 31, 2027. Phased retirement starts July 31, 2026, when creating new blueprint definitions will no longer be supported.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Microsoft a Leader in The Forrester Wave™ for Endpoint Management Platforms
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in Forrester Wave: Endpoint Management Platforms, Q2 2026, and reports the highest scores in the current offering and strategy categories.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Red Hat Enterprise Linux runner images are now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub-hosted larger runners now support Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 images in public preview. The images were introduced in partnership with Red Hat and are available for organizations to use.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available after a public preview that began in March 2026. GitHub says it has added several improvements since preview, including model selection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Cost centers now support enterprise teams
item.description:
GitHub cost centers now support adding enterprise teams as resources, so usage can be attributed according to your team structure. This update extends cost attribution for enterprises beyond individual resources.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers – Inference gateway
item.description:
Application Gateway for Containers is adding a preview inference gateway capability. It brings the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension to support AI inference traffic handling for Kubernetes workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on WG Device Management
item.description:
The Device Management WG is working on Kubernetes support for GPUs, TPUs, NICs, and other specialized hardware through Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), which graduated to GA in Kubernetes 1.34. The group is now expanding DRA and related APIs for sharing, topology-aware scheduling, health monitoring, and multi-node device use.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: security: CNAPP evolution: How Microsoft aligns with leading cloud risk management platforms
item.description:
Microsoft’s post says CNAPP platforms are increasingly used to prioritize exploitable risks, reduce exposure, and embed security across the application lifecycle. It positions Microsoft’s approach as aligned with other leading cloud risk management platforms.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Self-service credential revocation for incident response
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise owners can now use a new break-glass capability to immediately revoke all credentials for a compromised account or stolen credentials during incident response. The feature is self-service and intended for urgent security handling.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: StealC and Amadey: Breaking down infostealers and the cybercrime services that deliver them
item.description:
Microsoft’s DCU helped disrupt domains supporting the StealC and Amadey infrastructure on June 24, 2026. The post provides a technical overview of the StealC and Amadey malware families and the cybercrime services used to deliver them.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files migration assistant
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files migration assistant is in preview and available generally, using SnapMirror for data migration to ANF. It supports migrations from on-premises systems and from CVO or other cloud providers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds extended metadata for Replicate secrets
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning now adds extended metadata when it detects Replicate secrets, giving more context about leaked credentials. The change applies to the Replicate secret pattern and is meant to improve incident response and triage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Fetch Code Quality findings via REST API
item.description:
GitHub has added repository-level REST APIs for Code Quality findings in public preview. The new read-only endpoints expose code quality data via API, bringing parity closer to the GitHub UI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automatic Dependabot access to GitHub-hosted registries
item.description:
Dependabot can now read from private GitHub Packages registries without a personal access token when the package has granted repository access through “Manage Actions access.” This removes the need to configure a PAT for that dependency source.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot CLI: New terminal interface is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI’s redesigned terminal interface is now generally available. It adds a tabbed layout for working with GitHub directly from the terminal.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Deprecation of Python 3.9 for Dependabot
item.description:
Dependabot no longer supports Python 3.9 because it has reached end of life. Continuing to use Python 3.9 may prevent Dependabot from creating pull requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Agent Skills - Towards Autonomous Development, Deployment, and Validation🔥
item.description:
The article is a short note titled “Agent Skills - Towards Autonomous Development, Deployment, and Validation” with the phrase “aka, don’t ask me until prod.” No substantive technical details are provided in the supplied content.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app support for BYOK
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports bring your own key (BYOK), allowing agent sessions to use customer-managed model providers. Supported providers include OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic, and more.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Guarding AI memory
item.description:
Microsoft Security Blog discusses risks to AI memory and outlines defenses against attacks that target what an AI system remembers. The post is a high-level security overview rather than a product release note.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: One intrusion, two cyberattackers: Uncovering parallel threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft describes a ransomware case where two threat actors operated in parallel during the same intrusion, using overlapping tactics and evasion methods. The report emphasizes that isolated telemetry can miss complex attacks when activity from multiple actors is blended together.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: New features and Claude as agent provider preview in JetBrains IDEs
item.description:
GitHub added support for organization and enterprise agents in JetBrains IDEs, along with Copilot CLI message queueing/steering and a new agent debug logs summary view. The update also previews Claude as an agent provider in JetBrains IDEs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Where the agent decides, and where the tools actually run
item.description:
The article frames a design question about where to place an agent’s decision-making logic in an application that already has a deterministic state machine, tool integrations, and CI/CD. It focuses on separating the “brain” (judgment) from the “hands” (tool execution) within a graph/state-based architecture.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: 🖥️ GitHub Copilot App is Generally Available
item.description:
GitHub has announced that the GitHub Copilot app is now generally available on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Previously available as a technical preview for paid Copilot subscribers, the app is now open to all paid Copilot plans without restrictions.

What is the GitHub Copilot app

The GitHub Copilot app is a native desktop application purpose-built for agent-driven development. Unlike IDE extensions that augment a text editor, this app is a standalone environment where you direct AI agents across your full development lifecycle: from triaging an issue through to merging the resulting pull request, without switching between a terminal, browser, and IDE.

item.title: commandline: The durable asset is the loop you own. OpenEnv is its protocol.
item.description:
The article argues that the durable asset in agentic AI is the learning loop, not the rented model, and presents OpenEnv as the protocol for reinforcement learning environments. It positions OpenEnv around owning and standardizing the environment/evaluation loop for recursive self-improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: AI credits consumed per user now in the Copilot usage metrics API
item.description:
The Copilot usage metrics API now includes per-user AI credits consumed per day. The new data is derived from the same AI credits consumption source used by the usage-based billing API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: Maximising Copilot Token Efficiency 🚀
item.description:
With GitHub Copilot shifting to usage-based billing, every token in an agentic session now carries real cost. The good news? GitHub and Microsoft have spent months engineering the Copilot harness to be smarter about how it spends those tokens. This guide walks you through the key efficiency improvements, along with practical habits that will help your credits go further.
